$ xref path

Shortest call chains from function FROM to function TO over direct calls, tail jumps and pointer slots.

Finds shortest call chains between two functions and prints indented caller/callee trees annotated with panic source locations.

Usage

xref path [OPTIONS] <FROM> <TO>

Arguments and options

Arguments

<FROM>
Function where chains start (address or symbol name).
<TO>
Function where chains end (address or symbol name).

Options

--depth <DEPTH>
Maximum call-chain depth (hops).
default 8
--with-observed <WITH_OBSERVED>
Explicit observed-edge store tied to this binary; sample counts are not call counts.

Examples

All examples were recorded on public binaries; see Provenance.

Path 0xc7fc0 0x160bb0

Shortest call chains from 0xc7fc0 to 0x160bb0 with exact call-site addresses.

Command
$ xref -b xref.stripped path 0xc7fc0 0x160bb0
Output
0xc7fc0 -> 0x160bb0  (via 0xcf3cc)
0xc7fc0 -> 0xc7d60 -> 0x160bb0  (via 0xc8157, 0xc7fba)
0xc7fc0 -> 0xb43a0 -> 0x160bb0  (via 0xcea2e, 0xbafa7)
0xc7fc0 -> 0xc7d60 -> 0x124d50 -> 0x160bb0  (via 0xc8157, 0xc7e18, 0x124e0c)
0xc7fc0 -> 0x123950 -> 0x124d50 -> 0x160bb0  (via 0xcd2ae, 0x123b30, 0x124e0c)
0xc7fc0 -> 0xb43a0 -> 0xd5120 -> 0x160bb0  (via 0xcea2e, 0xb51e7, 0xd52b4)
0xc7fc0 -> 0xb43a0 -> 0xb3f00 -> 0x160bb0  (via 0xcea2e, 0xb7d23, 0xb41f6)
0xc7fc0 -> 0xb43a0 -> 0xc7d60 -> 0x160bb0  (via 0xcea2e, 0xba676, 0xc7fba)
8 paths
stderr
xref: load 1.9ms, total 5.0ms

Reading the output

  • One line per call chain from FROM to TO, shortest first, with the call sites that make each hop (via …). The last line counts the paths.
  • With 0 paths, the next lines say how many functions are reachable from FROM within --depth - 1 hops and how many indirect calls in them have no static target (call [rax+0x20] through a dyn-trait vtable, a closure or a function pointer), nearest first with their hop. Any of them can lead to TO, so 0 paths then means "no chain xref can see", not "unreachable".
  • After that, the other side: how many functions reach TO within --depth hops, and which of them can be entered indirectly at all, because their address is taken (held in a pointer slot or vtable record that code reads as data or that is never named directly, or loaded by code with lea). Slots that code only calls through are already followed as edges and are not listed. With no such entry, no chain of that depth exists; otherwise each entry names the slot or the code that takes its address, and xref callers ENTRY shows who.

Limits

  • Chains use direct calls, tail jumps and pointer slots xref can see, including a register loaded from a slot and called later (mov r12, [slot] ... call r12, with no write to the register in between, in code order). Calls through run-time pointers can hide a path; the 0 paths report lists them.
  • --depth bounds the chain length.

Provenance

Recorded with a development build of xref after 0.5.0 (path: unfollowed indirect calls) on Linux x86-64, on xref.stripped = a stripped xref build (the binary of the home-page examples). Output is unchanged except that whitespace at the end of each line and empty lines at the end of the output are removed; long outputs are cut where marked.
